extracted.intended_audience: advanced_undergraduate or graduate students in enumerative combinatorics/poset_and_lattice_theory
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of textbook exercises about posets, distributive and meet-distributive lattices, order ideals, rank-generating functions, Möbius functions, linear extensions, chromatic polynomials, and related enumerative invariants in combinatorics. Tasks range from concrete counts to structural and algebraic proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42(a) - Γ operator convergence (pairwise replacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite lattice L and f : L → N with positive values at chosen incomparable s,t, define operator Γf that replaces values at s,t by certain formulas (Γf(s)=f(s)/(f(s)+1), etc.); show that iterating Γ eventually stabilizes: for some n>0, Γ^n f = Γ^{n+1} f, i.e., the result is supported on a chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct Γf explicitly. Show termination/stabilization after finitely many steps; the limit function is supported on a chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42(b) - Uniqueness of limiting ˜f iff distributive
rubrics_metrics.description: Show the limiting function ˜f = Γ^n f (supported on a chain) does not depend on the order in which incomparable pairs are chosen iff L is distributive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove both directions: distributive ⇒ independence of choice; non-distributive ⇒ dependence. Use properties of join/meet to track effects of pairwise operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42(c) - Description of ˜f via join-irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming (b), show ˜f is the unique function L → N supported on a chain such that for all join-irreducibles t (with ˆ0 ≤ t) we have f(s) = sum_{t ≤ s} ˜f(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate original f to the chain-supported ˜f by summing over join-irreducibles; uniqueness follows from invertibility of triangular system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42(d) - Construct g(t) and order join-irreducibles to deduce structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Define g(t) from f-values on join-irreducibles and order them t1,...,tm so that g(t1) ≥ g(t2) ≥ ... ≥ g(tm); deduce ˜f(ui)=g(ti) for certain ui and ˜f(u)=0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly order join-irreducibles and construct the chain elements ui as joins of leading join-irreducibles; derive ˜f values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 42(e) - Boolean algebra example with excedance map to ˜f
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L = B_n; define f(S) = number of permutations w ∈ S_n with excedance set Exc(w) = S. Show that the limiting ˜f is concentrated on a chain of certain subsets and compute sums (example verifies ˜f sums to n!).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use excedance-set combinatorics and the Γ-process description from earlier parts to deduce resulting chain and compute values; show total equals n!.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 43 - Rank-generating function for Jf(Jf(P)) (specific P)
rubrics_metrics.description: For poset P described (elements si, ti with certain covers), find a nice product formula for the rank-generating function F_{Jf(Jf(P))}(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze poset structure, compute order ideals/join-irreducibles, and derive closed/formula product for generating function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 44(a) - Construct Pw from permutation w and count order ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Given permutation w = a1...an, define poset P_w as subset of [n]×[n] with order conditions (i,ai) relation; show j(P_w) equals number of order ideals of P_w and derive formula involving n!, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret inversion/position conditions as poset relations; count ideals via permutation statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 44(b) - Construct Qw and compute j(Qw)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Q_w on pairs (i,j) with conditions i<j and ai<aj; order accordingly and show j(Q_w) = (n+1)^n / Π i! (or other explicit formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate combinatorial structure of Q_w into factorial product enumeration; use combinatorial arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 45(a) - Polynomiality of L_k(n) for B_n
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L_k(n) be the number of k-element order ideals of B_n (boolean algebra). Show L_k(n) is a polynomial in n of degree k with leading coefficient 1/k!; differences ∆^i L_k(0) are nonnegative integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial interpretations to prove polynomiality and positivity of forward differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 45(b) - Explicit polynomials L_k(n) for small k
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute L_0,...,L_11(n) formulas (given) and note conjecture about real zeros fails for k=11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify given polynomial expressions and note counterexample to real-rootedness conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 46(a) - Sublattices of B_n count = partial orders on [n]
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(n) be number of sublattices of rank n of B_n. Show f(n) equals the number of partial orders P on [n].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish bijection between sublattices and partial orders (principal ideals/closure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 46(b) - Generating functions F(x), G(x) relation for sublattices containing ˆ0,ˆ1
rubrics_metrics.description: Let g(n) count sublattices of B_n containing ˆ0 and ˆ1. Show relation between generating functions F(x) and G(x), specifically G(x) = F(e^x - 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exponential generating functions and combinatorial constructions (set partitions) to relate counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 46(c) - Nonempty sublattices generating function H(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let h(n) number of nonempty sublattices of B_n; show H(x) = e^{2x} G(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine previous exponential generating function identities and inclusion/exclusion on presence of ˆ0,ˆ1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 47(a) - Meet-distributive lattices are lower semimodular and graded
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that any meet-distributive lattice (intervals where bottom equals meet of covers of top give boolean intervals) is lower semimodular and hence graded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use definition of meet-distributive to prove covering/rank properties that imply lower semimodularity and grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 47(b) - fk and gk relation in meet-distributive lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: For meet-distributive meet-semilattice L, let f_k be number of intervals isomorphic to B_k and g_k number of elements that cover exactly k elements. Show generating-function relation Σ g_k (1+x)^k = Σ f_k x^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count contributions by intervals and cover-degrees; deduce coefficient identities including alternating sum equals 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 47(c) - Consequence alternating sum equals 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce from (b) that Σ (-1)^k f_k = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plug x=-1 into generating identity and simplify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 47(d) - Compute fk and gk for specific lattice J(m×n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L = J(m×n) from part (a); compute explicit formulas for f_k and g_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use product structure and counting of boolean intervals and cover-degrees in the distributive lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 47(e)-(g) - Zeta/order polynomials equality for P_{mn} and Q_{mn}
rubrics_metrics.description: Define posets P_{mn} and Q_{mn} as certain subposets of P×P with index conditions; show they have the same zeta polynomial and order polynomial, and J(P_{mn}), J(Q_{mn}) have the same fk and gk values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bijections or algebraic manipulations showing polynomial invariance and matching interval counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 48 - Number of join-irreducibles below element by rank
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be meet-distributive lattice. For t ∈ L, show the number of join-irreducibles s ≤ t with s ρ(t) equals rank ρ(t) of t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structure of meet-distributive lattice to count join-irreducibles covering relations and ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 49 - L_p of natural partial orders is meet-distributive
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L_p denote set of all natural partial orders on [p] ordered by refinement; show L_p is meet-distributive and has rank p choose 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze refinement order, covering relations, and boolean interval property to verify meet-distributivity and compute rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 50 - Symmetry relation for covering numbers u(i,j), v(i,j)
rubrics_metrics.description: For finitary distributive lattice L with finitely many elements per rank, let u(i,j) be number of elements of rank i that cover exactly j elements, and v(i,j) number of elements of rank i covered by exactly j elements. Show relation Σ_{k≥0} (k choose j) u(i,k) = Σ_{k≥0} (k choose j) v(i-j,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial double counts or incidence algebra to relate covering and covered distributions across ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 51(a) - Uniqueness of finitary distributive lattice with given cover function
rubrics_metrics.description: Define cover function f (natural numbers → N) for finitary distributive lattice L by: if t covers i elements then t is covered by f(i) elements. Show there is at most one (up to iso) finitary distributive lattice with given f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove uniqueness by reconstructing poset from cover function iteratively using rank constraints and distributivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 51(b) - Finite distributive lattice with cover function implies boolean algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Show if L is finite distributive lattice with cover function f then L is a boolean algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finiteness and cover-degree constraints to force complementedness and boolean structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 51(c)-(d) - Existence/nonexistence of lattices with certain cover functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct finitary distributive lattices with cover functions f(n)=k and f(n)=n+k; show impossibility for f(n)=a n + k when a≥2 and k∈N with a≥2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit constructions (e.g., product/union constructions) and impossibility proofs based on combinatorial constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 51(e) - Classification of cover functions (seven classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show f(n) is cover function of a finitary distributive lattice L iff it belongs to one of seven specified classes (listing omitted), values of f on some small n determine isomorphism class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove necessary and sufficient conditions by analyzing how cover-degrees propagate in distributive lattices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 52 - Maximum e(P) for connected n-element poset
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine maximum possible number e(P) of linear extensions for a connected n-element poset P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find extremal poset(s) maximizing linear extensions and prove optimality (likely chain vs antichain considerations under connectivity constraint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 53 - Simplify sums f(P) and g(P) over order ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite poset P, simplify f(P) = Σ_{I∈J(P)} e(I) e(ḠI) and g(P) = Σ_{I∈J(P)} e(I) e(ḠI) / (#I), where ḠI is complement of order ideal I. Provide simplifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply combinatorial identities and properties of linear extensions to collapse sums; use symmetry between ideals and complements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 54 - Sum over chains with terminal maximal element
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify sum over all nonempty chains t1<...<tn with tn maximal: Σ 1/((#V_{t1}-1)(#V_{t2}-#V_{t1})...1). Generalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret telescoping product or probabilistic/inclusion arguments to simplify; generalize to other chain-dependent rational sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 55(a) - Maximize linear extensions for tree orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tree T on [n] and orientation o, let P(T,o) be transitive closure. Show e(P(T,o)) is maximized when o is bipartite (orientations giving no 3-chains), i.e., alternating orientation yielding at most 2-poset structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counting arguments for linear extensions and tree structure; compare orientations and show bipartite gives maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 55(b) - Extension to bipartite graphs open question
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask whether the result in (a) holds when T is replaced by any finite bipartite graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is posed as an open/extended problem; attempt counterexamples or proofs using graph structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 56 - Partition into saturated chains product of Fibonacci/Lucas
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(P) be number of partitions of poset P into disjoint saturated chains; if every element covers ≤2 and is covered by ≤2 elements, show f(P) is product of Fibonacci and Lucas numbers; compute f(m×n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local chain-decomposition recurrences and bijections to Fibonacci/Lucas structures; compute product decomposition for grid posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 57(a) - Lower bound for e(P) using λ_t (local order ideal sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n-element poset P and t∈P set λ_t = # {s∈P : s ≤ t}; show e(P) ≥ n! / Π_t λ_t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use probabilistic/inequality arguments counting linear extensions constrained by local sizes to get product lower bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 57(b) - Characterize equality condition as rooted-tree components
rubrics_metrics.description: Show equality in (3.115) holds iff each component of P is a rooted tree (with root maximum element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove necessity and sufficiency by analyzing when multiplicative lower bound is tight, tying to tree structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 58 - Decomposition of e(P) via antichain intersecting every maximal chain
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is antichain intersecting every maximal chain of P, show e(P) = Σ_{t∈A} e(P_t) where P_t are certain contractions; seek bijective proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide combinatorial bijection partitioning linear extensions by which element from A appears in certain position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 59 - Decomposition of poset via adding relation or identifying elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For incomparable s,t in p-element poset P, define P_{s<t}, P_{s>t}, P_{s=t} and show relation e(P) = e(P_{s<t}) + e(P_{s>t}) + e(P_{s=t}). Recurse until decomposition into chains; show independence of coefficients and give combinatorial interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive decomposition of poset into signed sums; interpret coefficients as multiplicities counting linear extensions of quotient chain types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 60(a) - Dropless labelings contain linear extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Define dropless labeling bijection f:P→[p] with no descent of the form s<t and f(s)=f(t)+1. Show every linear extension of P is a dropless labeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that linear extension order forbids such adjacent-down steps; trivial inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 60(b) - Dropless labelings ↔ acyclic orientations of incomparability graph
rubrics_metrics.description: Show number of dropless labelings equals number of acyclic orientations of incomparability graph inc(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct bijection between dropless labelings and acyclic orientations (orient edges based on relative labels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 60(c) - Bijective proof relating dropless labelings and certain bijections g:P→P
rubrics_metrics.description: Give bijection between dropless labelings of P and bijections g:P→P such that g(t)≥t (or never g(t)<t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 1.3.1(a) as hint and construct explicit mapping using order-preserving maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 61 - Composition poset chains count
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C be poset of all compositions ordered by covers that add 1 or split parts; for σ ∈ C count number of saturated chains from bottom composition (1) to σ in terms of familiar numbers; count total number of saturated chains to compositions of n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map composition refinement to combinatorial structures (Stirling numbers, factorials) and derive counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 62(a) - Rank-generating function for J(P_n)
rubrics_metrics.description: For poset P_n with chains s1<...<sn and t_i > s_i for all i (and certain cover relations), find expression for rank-generating function F(J(P_n), x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze poset product/union structure and derive closed-form generating function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 62(b)-(g) - Limits, formulas for e(P_n), order polynomial relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Study P = lim_{n→∞} P_n, compute e(P_n), express Ω_{P_n}(m) in terms of Stirling numbers of second kind (and first kind for other parts), define UP,m(x) generating function for protruded partitions and show product formula for UP,m(x) and rational generating functions P(q,x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial decompositions into partitions and known generating functions for Stirling numbers; deduce product forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 63-65 (chain/ surjective map enumerations) - Enumerative identities for surjective order-preserving maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Various exercises: for p-element poset P with every maximal chain length ℓ, enumerate surjective and strict surjective order-preserving maps to [s], show identities relating sums of e(P) with binomial coefficients and surjection counts; derive parity and chain-count consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Corollary 3.15.18, inclusion-exclusion on surjections, and parity arguments for surjective mapping counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 66(a)-(d) - Zigzag poset Zn order ideals, generating functions, counts
rubrics_metrics.description: For zigzag poset Zn, (a) count order ideals, (b) compute W_n(q) rank-gen function and find generating function F(x)=Σ W_n(q) x^n, (c) find e(Z_n), (d) find recurrence for Ω_{Z_n}(m) generating functions G_m(x) with initial conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit alternating cover structure to derive explicit formulas/recurrences; derive closed generating functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 67 - Linear extensions count for poset P_{p,q}
rubrics_metrics.description: For poset P_{p,q} made of three chains with comparabilities si<ui and ti<ui, compute e(P_{p,q}) with explicit factorial product formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hook-length style or multinomial counts to derive closed factorial formula as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 68(a)-(c) - Garland poset Gn counts and alternating labelings
rubrics_metrics.description: For garland/double-fence Gn compute generating functions j(n,k) for k-element order ideals, show e(Gn) equals number of alternating labelings of 2×n chain, and find formula/generating function for e(Gn) (values given for n≤6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate to alternating permutations/alternating labelings and derive explicit generating function or recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 69(a)-(b) - Log-concavity of Pt(x) and fraction bounds for pair occurrences
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For fixed t in p-element poset P, polynomial P_t(x)=Σ_{f∈L(P)} x^{f(t)} is log-concave. (b) If P not a chain, show existence of s,t with specified lower/upper bounds on fraction of linear extensions with f(s)<f(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real-rootedness/log-concavity results and probabilistic counting on linear extensions; quantify fractions using Fibonacci/golden ratio bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 70(a)-(c) - Even-sum subsets poset and µ-values generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: For En subsets with even sum ordered by inclusion, (a) count #En, (b) compute µ(S,T) for S≤T in En, (c) generalize to P_k subsets with sum divisible by k and express µ via exponential generating function using primitive kth root of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use character sums/modular roots of unity and inclusion-exclusion to express Möbius values and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 71 - Free distributive lattice FD(P) is J(J(P))
rubrics_metrics.description: Show FD(P) (free distributive lattice on P) is isomorphic to J(J(P)) and derive finiteness statements, and prove sublattice M(P) correspondences in later parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use universal property of free distributive lattices and representation as order ideals of order-ideal poset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 72(a)-(b) - M(P) sublattice of J(P) and representation theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Show set of order ideals of P corresponding to antichains of fixed size forms sublattice M_k(P) of J(P). (b) Show every finite distributive lattice is isomorphic to M(P) for some P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct P from join-irreducibles; use Birkhoff representation and antichain-to-ideal correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 73(a)-(b) - GP(q,x) and product formula for ordinal product
rubrics_metrics.description: Define G_P(q,x)=Σ_{I} q^{#I} x^{m(I)} over order ideals I. Show GP⊗Q(q,x)=G_P(qn, q^{-n}(G_Q(q,x))) where ⊗ is ordinal product; deduce simple formula when |P|=p: G_P(q,1)=q^{p}/(1-q)^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial decomposition of ideals in ordinal product and algebra of generating functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 74 - Binary stopping rules lattice Ln and recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Define poset Ln of binary stopping rules of length n ordered by 'never stop later'; show Ln is distributive, compute join-irreducibles, and find recurrence for rank-generating function F(L_n,q) in terms of F(L_{n-1},q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model stopping rules by prefix trees/trie structure; deduce distributive lattice structure and recurrence via adding a toss step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 75(a)-(c) - Poset of acyclic orientations ao(G,v) is poset with distributive components
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix connected graph G and vertex v; define partial order on acyclic orientations with v sink via source-pushing operations. (a) Show (ao(G,v),≤) is a poset. (b) For 6-cycle classify as J(2×2)+4+4+1+1. (c) Show every connected component is distributive lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze source-pushing operations as cover relations, use graph symmetry, and decompose into distributive components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 76(a)-(d) - Incidence algebra radicals, ideals, automorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For locally finite posets P and Q and incidence algebra I(P) over field K: (a) Jacobson radical comprises functions f with f(t,t)=0; (b) lattice of two-sided ideals is isomorphic to order ideals of Int(P) by reverse inclusion; (c) I(P) ≅ I(Q) ⇒ P ≅ Q as posets; (d) describe group of K-automorphisms and K-derivations of I(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use algebraic structure of incidence algebras, properties of idempotents and ideals, and structural invariants to prove isomorphism-sensitivity and characterize automorphisms/derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 77(a)-(f) - Greene-Kleitman partition λ and µ, conjugacy and Dilworth
rubrics_metrics.description: Define λ_i as maximum size of union of i chains and µ_i similarly for antichains; show λ is partition with λ_1≥... and µ = λ' (conjugate). Deduce Dilworth's theorem and related equalities, matrix/Jordan form characterization, and other consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chain/antichain union extremal definitions, conjugation arguments, and linear-algebraic interpretations (Jordan blocks) to prove equivalences and corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 78(a)-(c) - Compute λ and µ for B_n, Π_n, and Par(n) dominance lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine partitions λ and µ for boolean algebra B_n, partition lattice Π_n, and partition dominance lattice Par(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze chain and antichain structures in these classical lattices to compute extremal union sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 79 - P-domino tableaux, comajor index, self-evacuating extensions equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: For labeled poset P on [p], show equivalence of (i) certain sum of major/comajor indices over linear extensions ≡ quantity w(P), (ii) number of P-domino tableaux, and (iii) number of self-evacuating linear extensions; tie parity conditions for p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate descent/comajor statistics to domino tilings and evacuation symmetry using combinatorial bijections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 80(a)-(b) - Promotion operator periodicity on special posets
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For posets of types (i) rectangles, (ii) shifted double staircases, (iii) shifted trapezoids, show promotion ∂^p leaves linear extensions invariant. (b) For staircase poset, show ∂^p corresponds to reflecting labeling (so ∂^{2p}=id).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structural symmetries of poset shapes and properties of promotion to prove invariance/periodicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 81(a)-(b) - Sign-balanced posets criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A poset is sign-balanced if linear extensions split evenly between even/odd permutations. (a) If every nonminimal element is greater than ≥2 minimal elements, show P sign-balanced. (b) If length of every maximal chain congruent to n (mod 2), show P sign-balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide parity and involution arguments on linear extensions to balance sign counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 82 - Product of two chains sign-balanced criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Show product of two chains p×q is sign-balanced iff p,q>1 and p q ≡ ? (mod 2) (explicit condition given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze parity of permutations corresponding to linear extensions and deduce criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 83 - Sign-balanced criterion via absence of P-domino tableau
rubrics_metrics.description: Show P is sign-balanced if |P| is even and there does not exist a P-domino tableau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use domino tiling interpretation to produce involution on linear extensions reversing parity when tilings absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 84 - Closure operators, quotient poset Möbius relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given closure operator ¯ on locally finite poset P producing quotient P, show relation µ_P(s,u) summed over u with same closure relates to µ_{quotient}(¯s,¯t), with explicit cases when s is closed or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum Möbius values on fiber of quotient map and use properties of closure to collapse sums; rigorous case analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 85 - Equivalence of odd-atom and odd-coatom conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove for finite poset P that intervals [s,t] all have odd number of atoms iff all intervals have odd number of coatoms; hint use µ modulo 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Möbius function parity properties and reciprocity between atoms and coatoms via Möbius values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 86 - Inversion formula for functions on finite lattice using Möbius algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Given functions f,g on finite lattice L satisfying f(s)=Σ_{t≥s} g(t), show inversion formula g(s)=Σ_t α(s,t) f(t) with explicit coefficient α(s,t)=Σ_{u≥t} µ(s,u)µ(t,u)/µ(0,u) when µ(0,u)=0 condition absent etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Möbius inversion and properties of µ to derive explicit rational-linear combination inversion; handle denominators carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 87(a)-(d) - Product identities for Möbius-weighted sums and incidence algebra proof
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For finite poset with µ, show product identity for Σ (f(t)-1) over chains equals Σ (-1)^{k+1} µ(0,t1)µ(t1,t2)... f(t1)...f(tk). (b) Deduce particular identity when summing f over whole poset. (c) Provide incidence-algebra proof. (d) Deduce equation (3.113) for meet-distributive lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand multiplicative telescoping sums and apply Möbius inversion; present both combinatorial and algebraic proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 88 - Sum of µ(s,t) over s ≤ t equals 1
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite poset with 0 and 1, show Σ_{t ≥ s} µ(s,t) = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straightforward application of Möbius inversion to constant function; present direct proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 89 - f_L(m) count of m-tuples with meet 0 equals Σ µ(0,t) (#V_t)^m
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite lattice L, let f_L(m) count m-tuples whose meet is 0; show f_L(m)=Σ_{t∈L} µ(0,t) (|V_t|)^m. Give two proofs: direct Möbius inversion and via Möbius algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret indicator of meet-0 as Möbius-inverted sum and apply algebraic convolution viewpoint for alternative proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 90 - f and inverse in incidence algebra for graded poset
rubrics_metrics.description: For graded finite poset P with m(s,t) number of maximal chains, define f(s,t)=m(s,t)/ℓ(s,t)! and show f^{-1}(s,t)=(-1)^{ℓ(s,t)} f(s,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial sign-reversal on chains and factorial normalization to show inverse under convolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 91(a)-(b) - Bounds on |µ(0,1)| in terms of number of atoms and chain length
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For finite lattice with n atoms show |µ(0,1)| ≤ C(n) with explicit best-possible bound. (b) If longest chain length ≤ ℓ then bound |µ(0,1)| ≤ something depending on n and ℓ, best possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rank/antichain constraints and extremal constructions to derive tight bounds on Möbius absolute value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 92 - Decomposition of µ(0,1) via complements of fixed element
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix t in finite lattice L and show µ(0,1)=Σ_{u,v} µ(0,u) ζ(u,v) µ(v,1) where u,v range over complements of t; deduce if µ(0,1)=0 then L is not complemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use complement identities and Möbius/zetafunction relations to express global µ via contributions from complements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 93(a)-(b) - Complemented lattice condition via even intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If for every t>0 the interval [0,t] has even cardinality, show lattice is complemented. (b) Provide simple proof avoiding Möbius functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parity and pairing arguments to produce complements for each element; supply constructive proof avoiding Möbius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 94 - Valuations on finite distributive lattice determined by join-irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: For L=J(P) finite distributive, show valuation v:L→C with v(0)=0 and v(s)+v(t)=v(s∨t)+v(s∧t) is uniquely determined by its values on join-irreducibles (P). Provide formula v(I)=Σ_{t∈I} v(t) µ(t,1) for order ideal I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Möbius inversion on poset of ideals and property of valuations to express v in terms of join-irreducibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 95 - Möbius-algebra identity involving fixed z
rubrics_metrics.description: In Möbius algebra of finite lattice L show identity Σ_{t} µ(0,t) t = Σ_{u≤z} µ(0,u) u · (Σ_{v≤z} µ(0,v) v) where product interpreted appropriately; (exercise gives formal identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulate Möbius-algebra relations and use convolution to prove identity; careful with algebraic sum/product order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 96(a)-(f) - Determinant identity and combinatorial consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For function f(s,v) define F(s,v)=Σ_{u≤s} f(u,v) and show determinant identity det[F(s∧t,s)]_{s,t∈L} = Π_{s∈L} f(s,s). (b) Deduce determinant of gcd(i,j) matrix equals Π φ(k). (c)-(f) Consequences: existence of permutation w such that meet with w(s) is 0, rank inequalities in geometric lattices, modularity condition if equality holds, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use triangularization and LU-decompositions in incidence algebra to deduce determinant factorization; apply to algebraic/combinatorial contexts for consequences on geometric lattices and permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 97 - Permutation with complements for finite lattice when µ(t,1)=0
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L finite lattice with µ(0,t)=0 for all t with rank ≤k; show existence of permutation w:L→L such that for all t, t and w(t) are complements; show stronger/false statements when assumptions weakened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct matching between elements and complements via Hall's theorem or determinant argument and show counterexamples when conditions fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 98 - Inequality for Möbius values and η(t) in geometric lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L finite geometric lattice and t a coatom. Let η(t) be number of atoms not ≤ t. Show |µ(0,1)| ≤ 6 |µ(0,t)| / η(t) (explicit inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate Möbius values across coatoms using geometric lattice properties and atom counts to bound ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 99 - α(L,f) count equals (−1)^n µ(0,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: In finite geometric lattice L of rank n let L′=L−{ˆ0} and f:L′→A mapping elements to atoms ≤ t; count α(L,f) maximal chains t0<...<tn with f(t1)∨...∨f(tn)=1 and show α(L,f)=(−1)^n µ(0,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Möbius inversion and geometric lattice coverage by atoms to count such maximal chains; sign alternation due to rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 100(a)-(d) - Atoms meet coatoms, Möbius alternation, boolean intervals, finite geometric lattice classification
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Show every element in finite geometric lattice is meet of coatoms. (b) Improve Prop: Möbius function alternates in sign with rank. (c) If µ(s,t)=±1 then [s,t] is boolean. (d) Classification: for any fixed n there are finitely many geometric lattices not isomorphic to Li×Bd for some i,d; prove existence of such finite family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use properties of geometric lattices (atomistic, semimodular) and Möbius combinatorics to deduce alternation and boolean-interval characterizations; classify via rank/atomicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 101(a)-(c) - Injective maps between subsets in finite lattices and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Given finite lattice L and subsets A,B with property involving µ nonzero intervals, show existence of injective map φ:B→A with φ(s)≥s for all s. (b) For finite modular lattice K conclude K geometric when 1 is join of atoms etc., equal number atoms and coatoms, and ψ_b is lattice iso between intervals [a,b] and [b,a]. (c) For finite modular lattice deduce existence of injective map φ:J_k→M_k mapping elements covering ≤k to those covered by ≤k with φ(s)≥s; deduce parity equalities and give counterexample to P_k ≅ R_k in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Möbius-nonvanishing property to construct injections via combinatorial matching or Möbius inversion; apply modularity to derive interval isomorphisms and cover-count equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 102(a)-(b) - Existence of join-irreducible with small principal dual ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For finite lattice with n elements does there exist join-irreducible t such that principal dual ideal V_t has ≤ n/2 elements? (b) If some V_t > n/2, show µ(0,s)=0 for some s>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate distribution of principal dual ideals and use Möbius/cover arguments to deduce existence or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 103 - Extremal values of µ(0,1) given antichain meeting every maximal chain
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite lattice L with subset S of size n that is antichain and meets every maximal chain, find smallest and largest possible values of µ(0,1) as function of n; give examples and bounds (e.g., for n=2, n=3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct extremal lattices achieving bounds and prove optimality via Möbius function properties and chain/antichain constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 104(a)-(b) - Max possible µ(0,1) for poset with ˆ0,ˆ1 and fixed size
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For (n+2)-element poset with 0 and 1 what is largest possible |µ(0,1)|? (b) Same question for n-element lattices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find extremal configurations (antichain-like or lattice constructions) maximizing absolute Möbius value and prove optimality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 105 - Max |µ(0,1)| over posets with bounded cover number k and chain length ℓ
rubrics_metrics.description: For k,ℓ fixed, over posets with 0,1, max |µ(0,1)| subject to every element covered by ≤k elements and longest chain length ℓ; find maximum value and extremal posets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize Möbius absolute value under local degree and chain-length constraints; use extremal combinatorics to construct maximizing posets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 106 - Divisibility property for sizes of order ideals under µ vanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: If finite lattice L satisfies µ_L(t,u)=0 for any t,u with t≤u and µ(0,t)≠0, and I is order ideal of boolean algebra B_n of rank ≤k, show |I| divisible by 2^{2k+1} (?) (exercise states divisibility by 2^{2k+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Möbius vanishing constraints to deduce parity/divisibility conditions on sizes of certain ideals via algebraic counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 107 - Existence of element t with µ(0,t) divisible by large power of 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Given conditions (text truncated in chunk), show existence of t with certain divisibility (e.g., by 2^{2k+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow from previous exercise and parity/divisibility properties of Möbius values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 108(a)-(c) - Chromatic polynomial χ_G(n) and graphical arrangement relation
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Express chromatic polynomial χ_G(n) as Σ_{j} S_G(j) n^{ ar j} (stable partitions), deduce degree and leading coefficient and first lower coefficient equals −#E. (b) Let L_G be lattice of connected partitions of vertex set; show χ_G(n)=Σ_{π∈L_G} µ(0,π) n^{#π} so χ_G and characteristic polynomial χ_{L_G} relate by χ_G(n)= n^c χ_{L_G}(n) where c number connected components. (c) Show graphical hyperplane arrangement B_G has intersection poset isomorphic to L_G, deduce χ_G = χ_{B_G}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combinatorial partitioning into stable blocks, Möbius inversion on connected partition lattice, and hyperplane arrangement intersection theory to relate polynomials.
